Relations and Functions.sol: x + 1 = 3 gives x = 2 and y − 2 = 1 gives y = 3, so x + y = 5.

Relations and Functions.q: If n(A) = 2 and n(B) = 3, how many relations are there from A to B?
Relations and Functions.sol: A × B has 2 × 3 = 6 elements; every subset is a relation, so there are 2⁶ = 64 relations.

Permutations and Combinations.q: Consider the letters of the word COMMITTEE.

parts.q: (a) How many different arrangements of all the letters are there?
(b) How many of these arrangements begin with a vowel?

Permutations and Combinations.sol: (a) 9! divided by the factorials of the repeated letters = 45360. (b) Put each different vowel first in turn and arrange the remaining letters: 20160.

Permutations and Combinations.q: Consider the letters of the word ASSESS.

parts.q: (a) How many different arrangements of all the letters are there?
(b) How many of these arrangements begin with a vowel?

Permutations and Combinations.sol: (a) 6! divided by the factorials of the repeated letters = 30. (b) Put each different vowel first in turn and arrange the remaining letters: 10.

Binomial Theorem.q: Find the coefficient of x<sup>4</sup> in the expansion of (1 + 3x)<sup>8</sup>.
Binomial Theorem.sol: The term is <sup>8</sup>C<sub>4</sub>(3x)<sup>4</sup>, so the coefficient is 70 × 81 = 5670.

Binomial Theorem.q: Find the coefficient of x<sup>3</sup> in the expansion of (1 + 2x)<sup>9</sup>.
Binomial Theorem.sol: The term is <sup>9</sup>C<sub>3</sub>(2x)<sup>3</sup>, so the coefficient is 84 × 8 = 672.

Binomial Theorem.q: Find the coefficient of x<sup>2</sup> in the expansion of (1 + 2x)<sup>8</sup>.
Binomial Theorem.sol: The term is <sup>8</sup>C<sub>2</sub>(2x)<sup>2</sup>, so the coefficient is 28 × 4 = 112.

Binomial Theorem.q: Find the coefficient of x<sup>2</sup> in the expansion of (1 + x)<sup>8</sup>.
Binomial Theorem.sol: The term is <sup>8</sup>C<sub>2</sub>(x)<sup>2</sup>, so the coefficient is 28 × 1 = 28.

Binomial Theorem.q: Find the coefficient of x<sup>4</sup> in the expansion of (1 + 3x)<sup>5</sup>.
Binomial Theorem.sol: The term is <sup>5</sup>C<sub>4</sub>(3x)<sup>4</sup>, so the coefficient is 5 × 81 = 405.

Binomial Theorem.q: Find the coefficient of x<sup>2</sup> in the expansion of (1 + 2x)<sup>6</sup>.
Binomial Theorem.sol: The term is <sup>6</sup>C<sub>2</sub>(2x)<sup>2</sup>, so the coefficient is 15 × 4 = 60.

Straight Lines.q: Find the slope of the line through (−4, −4) and (−6, −6).
A straight line passes through (1, 6) and (3, 10).
Straight Lines.sol: (a) m = (10 − 6) / (3 − 1) = 2. (b) y = 2x + c through (1, 6) gives c = 4. (c) Putting y = 0 gives x = −2.

Straight Lines.q: Find the slope of the line through (−1, −2) and (1, 4).
A straight line passes through (−3, −3) and (−1, −5).
Straight Lines.sol: (a) m = (−5 − (−3)) / (−1 − (−3)) = −1. (b) y = −1x + c through (−3, −3) gives c = −6. (c) Putting y = 0 gives x = −6.

Straight Lines.q: Find the slope of the line through (3, −2) and (6, 2).

Probability.q: One card is drawn from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. Find the probability that it is a face card.
Probability.sol: There are 12 favourable cards, so the probability is 12/52 = 3/13.

Probability.q: One card is drawn from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. Find the probability that it is a king or a heart.

Relations and Functions.q: A relation R in a set A is called a ______ relation if R = A × A.
Relations and Functions.sol: If every element of A is related to every element of A, i.e. R = A × A, the relation is called the universal relation.

Relations and Functions.q: A function f : X → Y is said to be ______ if every element of Y is the image of some element of X under f.
Relations and Functions.sol: f is onto (surjective) if for every y ∈ Y there exists x ∈ X with f(x) = y, i.e. range = codomain.

Relations and Functions.q: How many ordered pairs are there in the identity relation on a set having 4 elements?
Relations and Functions.sol: The identity relation contains only the pairs (a, a), one for each element, so it has 4 pairs.

Relations and Functions.q: How many equivalence relations on the set {1, 2, 3} contain the ordered pair (1, 2)?
Relations and Functions.sol: 1 and 2 must be in the same class: either {1, 2}, {3} or {1, 2, 3}. So there are 2 such equivalence relations.

Relations and Functions.q: How many one-one functions are there from the set {1, 2, 3} to itself?
Relations and Functions.sol: A one-one function from a 3-element set to itself is a permutation, so there are 3! = 6.

Relations and Functions.q: On A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}, R = {(a, b) : |a − b| is even} is an equivalence relation. How many elements of A are related to 1 (including 1 itself)?
Relations and Functions.sol: |a − 1| is even for a = 1, 3, 5, so the equivalence class of 1 is {1, 3, 5}, which has 3 elements.

Application of Derivatives.q: The radius of a circular ink blot increases at 4 cm/s.

parts.q: (a) How fast is the area increasing when the radius is 12 cm (cm²/s)? You may leave π in your answer.
(b) How fast is the circumference increasing (cm/s)? You may leave π in your answer.
(c) What is the area when the radius is 12 cm (cm²)? You may leave π in your answer.

Application of Derivatives.sol: (a) dA/dt = 2πr × dr/dt = 2π × 12 × 4 = 96π cm²/s. (b) dC/dt = 2π × dr/dt = 8π cm/s. (c) A = π × 12² = 144π cm².

parts.q: (a) At what value of x does f have a local maximum?

Application of Derivatives.sol: f′(x) = 3x² − 6x − 24 = 3(x + 2)(x − 4). f′ changes from + to − at x = −2 (local maximum 23) and from − to + at x = 4 (local minimum −85).

parts.q: (a) Find the area bounded by the curve, the x-axis and the line x = 3.
(b) Find the area enclosed between the curve and the line y = 9x.

Application of Integrals.sol: (a) ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>3</sup> 3x² dx = 3 × 3³ / 3 = 27. (b) The curves meet at x = 0 and x = 3: ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>3</sup> (9x − 3x²) dx = 27/2.

parts.q: (a) Find the area bounded by the curve, the x-axis and the line x = 4.

parts.q: (a) Find the area bounded by the curve, the x-axis and the line x = 6.

Differential Equations.q: What is the order of the differential equation d²y/dx² + (dy/dx)³ + y = 0?
Differential Equations.sol: The highest order derivative present is d²y/dx², so the order is 2.

Differential Equations.q: What is the degree of the differential equation (d²y/dx²)³ + (dy/dx)⁴ + y = 0?
Differential Equations.sol: The equation is a polynomial in derivatives; the highest order derivative d²y/dx² occurs with power 3, so the degree is 3.

Differential Equations.q: How many arbitrary constants are there in the general solution of a differential equation of order 3?
Differential Equations.sol: The general solution of an nth order differential equation contains n arbitrary constants, so here 3.

Differential Equations.q: Find the sum of the order and the degree of the differential equation (d³y/dx³)² + (d²y/dx²)³ + dy/dx + y = 0.
Differential Equations.sol: Highest order derivative is d³y/dx³ (order 3), and its power is 2 (degree 2); 3 + 2 = 5.

Differential Equations.q: Solve dy/dx = 2x with y(0) = 1. What is the value of y when x = 3?
Differential Equations.sol: y = x² + C; y(0) = 1 gives C = 1, so y = x² + 1 and y(3) = 10.

Differential Equations.q: Solve dy/dx = y with y(0) = 2. What is the value of y when x = ln 3?
Differential Equations.sol: dy/y = dx gives y = Ce^x; y(0) = 2 gives C = 2, so y = 2e^(ln 3) = 6.
